es.summary: Enfermedad pulmonar crónica caracterizada por inflamación y estrechamiento reversible de las vías respiratorias, que produce sibilancias, tos y disnea. Los episodios agudos se denominan crisis asmática.
key_points: Inflamación de la mucosa bronquial y hiperreactividad bronquial
Broncoconstricción reversible es la base del ataque
Control de desencadenantes y uso correcto de inhaladores son esenciales
Corticosteroides inhalados son la base del tratamiento de mantenimiento

pathophysiology: Alérgeno o irritante activa mastocitos → liberación de mediadores inflamatorios
Inflamación de la mucosa bronquial → edema y aumento de secreción
Broncoconstricción por contracción del músculo liso bronquial
Hipersecreción de moco y atrapamiento de aire
risk_factors: Antecedentes familiares de asma o alergias
Exposición a ácaros, moho, pelos de mascotas, polen
Tabaquismo pasivo o contaminación del aire
Infecciones respiratorias frecuentes en la infancia
Obesidad y ejercicio en clima frío
signs_symptoms: Tos seca, peor por la noche o al ejercicio
Disnea de inicio súbito o progresiva
Uso de músculos accesorios y aleteo nasal
diagnostics: Espirometría: FEV1/FVC < 0.70 y reversibilidad >12% tras broncodilatador
Peak flow < 80% del valor esperado en crisis
Oxígeno arterial: PaO2 ≥ 80 mmHg en reposo, ↓ en crisis
Pruebas de alergia cutánea o IgE específica según sospecha
treatment: Broncodilatadores beta‑2 agonistas de acción corta (albuterol) – rescate
Broncodilatadores beta‑2 agonistas de acción prolongada (salmeterol) – mantenimiento
Educación, plan de acción y control de desencadenantes
complications: Remodelado bronquial crónico → disminución de la función pulmonar
Efectos adversos de corticoides (candidiasis oral, supresión adrenal)
nursing_care: Evaluar frecuencia respiratoria, uso de músculos accesorios y SpO2 cada 4 h
Administrar broncodilatador según orden y observar respuesta en 5‑15 min
Mantener posición semi‑sentada o Fowler para facilitar la expansión pulmonar
Monitorear signos de fatiga, nivel de conciencia y posible deterioro
Registrar pico de flujo y comparar con valores personales
patient_teaching: Enseñar técnica correcta de inhalador y uso del espaciador
Elaborar y practicar plan de acción para crisis
Registrar pico de flujo diario y reconocer valores de alerta
Revisar higiene bucal después de corticoides inhalados

outcomes: Patrón respiratorio eficaz: SpO2 ≥ 95% en reposo
Disminución de sibilancias a auscultación en 24 h

interventions.action: Administrar broncodilatador de acción corta según prescripción y evaluar respuesta en 5‑15 min
interventions.rationale: Relaja el músculo liso bronquial y mejora el flujo aéreo rápidamente

interventions.action: Colocar al paciente en posición semi‑sentada o Fowler
interventions.rationale: Facilita la expansión pulmonar y reduce el trabajo respiratorio

interventions.action: Monitorear SpO2 y frecuencia respiratoria cada 4 h o según cambios clínicos
interventions.rationale: Detecta deterioro temprano y permite intervención oportuna

interventions.action: Enseñar uso del espaciador y técnica de inhalación correcta
interventions.rationale: Optimiza la entrega del medicamento a los pulmones

interventions.action: Registrar pico de flujo y comparar con valores personales
interventions.rationale: Permite identificar empeoramiento antes de la crisis

evidenced_by: Fatiga al realizar actividades de la vida diaria
Limitación para caminar > 100 m sin pausa
outcomes: Capacidad para caminar 200 m sin disnea en 2 semanas
Nivel de actividad incrementado 20 % según escala de Borg

interventions.action: Planificar actividades graduales de ejercicio aeróbico bajo supervisión
interventions.rationale: Mejora la tolerancia al ejercicio y reduce la hiperreactividad

interventions.action: Enseñar uso del broncodilatador de acción corta antes del ejercicio
interventions.rationale: Previene la broncoconstricción inducida por actividad física

interventions.action: Monitorear signos vitales y SpO2 antes, durante y después del ejercicio
interventions.rationale: Detecta desaturación y permite ajustar la intensidad

interventions.action: Educar al paciente sobre reconocimiento de límites y descanso adecuado
interventions.rationale: Previene la exacerbación y promueve autocuidado

interventions.action: Reforzar adherencia al tratamiento de mantenimiento (corticoides inhalados)
interventions.rationale: Controla la inflamación subyacente y mejora la capacidad funcional

en.summary: Chronic lung disease characterized by inflammation and reversible narrowing of the airways, producing wheezing, cough, and dyspnea. Acute episodes are called asthma attacks.
key_points: Bronchial mucosal inflammation and bronchial hyperreactivity
Reversible bronchoconstriction is the basis of the attack
Trigger control and correct inhaler use are essential
Inhaled corticosteroids are the foundation of maintenance treatment

pathophysiology: Allergen or irritant activates mast cells → release of inflammatory mediators
Bronchial mucosal inflammation → edema and increased secretions
Bronchoconstriction from contraction of bronchial smooth muscle
Excess mucus secretion and air trapping
risk_factors: Family history of asthma or allergies
Exposure to dust mites, mold, pet dander, pollen
Obesity and exercise in cold weather
signs_symptoms: Dry cough, worse at night or with exercise
Use of accessory muscles and nasal flaring
diagnostics: Spirometry: FEV1/FVC < 0.70 and reversibility >12% after bronchodilator
Peak flow < 80% of expected value during crisis
Arterial oxygen: PaO2 ≥ 80 mmHg at rest, ↓ during crisis
Skin allergy tests or specific IgE as indicated
treatment: Education, action plan, and trigger control
complications: Chronic bronchial remodeling → decreased lung function
Side effects of steroids (oral candidiasis, adrenal suppression)
nursing_care: Assess respiratory rate, accessory muscle use, and SpO2 every 4 h
Administer bronchodilator per order and observe response in 5‑15 min
Maintain semi‑upright or Fowler position to aid lung expansion
Monitor for fatigue, level of consciousness, and possible deterioration
Record peak flow and compare with personal values
patient_teaching: Teach correct inhaler technique and spacer use
Develop and practice an action plan for attacks
Record daily peak flow and recognize warning values
Review oral hygiene after inhaled steroids

outcomes: Effective breathing pattern: SpO2 ≥ 95% at rest
Reduced wheezing on auscultation within 24 h

interventions.action: Administer short‑acting bronchodilator per prescription and assess response in 5‑15 min
interventions.rationale: Relaxes bronchial smooth muscle and quickly improves airflow

interventions.action: Place patient in semi‑upright or Fowler position
interventions.rationale: Facilitates lung expansion and reduces work of breathing

interventions.action: Monitor SpO2 and respiratory rate every 4 h or as clinically indicated
interventions.rationale: Detects early deterioration and allows timely intervention

interventions.action: Teach spacer use and correct inhalation technique
interventions.rationale: Optimizes drug delivery to the lungs

interventions.action: Record peak flow and compare with personal values
interventions.rationale: Identifies worsening before a crisis

evidenced_by: Fatigue during activities of daily living
Limited ability to walk > 100 m without pause
outcomes: Ability to walk 200 m without dyspnea in 2 weeks
Activity level increased 20% per Borg scale

interventions.action: Plan gradual aerobic exercise under supervision
interventions.rationale: Improves exercise tolerance and reduces hyperreactivity

interventions.action: Teach use of short‑acting bronchodilator before exercise
interventions.rationale: Prevents exercise‑induced bronchoconstriction

interventions.action: Monitor vital signs and SpO2 before, during, and after exercise
interventions.rationale: Detects desaturation and allows intensity adjustment

interventions.action: Educate patient on recognizing limits and adequate rest
interventions.rationale: Prevents exacerbation and promotes self‑care

interventions.action: Reinforce adherence to maintenance therapy (inhaled steroids)
interventions.rationale: Controls underlying inflammation and improves functional capacity

summary.1.quote: An asthma attack is also known as asthma exacerbation.

key_points.2.quote: Patient education topics include using an inhaler and peak flow meter, strategies to avoid triggers, and implementing an asthma action plan ( Figure 11.15 , Figure 11.16 , and Figure 11.17 ).

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: Mast cells release leukotrienes, histamine, and prostaglandins.

sections.pathophysiology.1.quote: Inflammation, further bronchoconstriction, and increased mucous production occur.

sections.pathophysiology.2.quote: These substances cause bronchoconstriction , meaning the smooth muscle in the airways constrict, narrowing the airway.

sections.pathophysiology.3.quote: Spirometry tests are also used to assess airway changes in response to bronchodilator administration; bronchodilators open narrowed airways and allow a significant increase in the volume of air that can be inhaled and forcefully exhaled.

sections.risk_factors.0.quote: Asthma is more common in patients with a family history of asthma and allergies.

sections.signs_symptoms.0.quote: Expiratory wheezes are the most common adventitious lung sound in asthma.

sections.signs_symptoms.1.quote: Often, the cough is worse at night.

sections.signs_symptoms.2.quote: Subjective data can include the presence of shortness of breath, wheezing, chest tightness, cough, increased mucus, activity limitations, and frequency of nighttime waking due to breathing difficulty.

sections.treatment.4.quote: In severe flares, oral or intravenous corticosteroids are often necessary to decrease inflammation.

sections.treatment.5.quote: Patient education topics include using an inhaler and peak flow meter, strategies to avoid triggers, and implementing an asthma action plan ( Figure 11.15 , Figure 11.16 , and Figure 11.17 ).

sections.patient_teaching.0.quote: This video provides important teaching points about how to use inhalers, nebulizers, spacers, and chambers.

sections.patient_teaching.1.quote: Identifying triggers and controlling exposure is important for patients with asthma.

sections.patient_teaching.2.quote: Patient education topics include using an inhaler and peak flow meter, strategies to avoid triggers, and implementing an asthma action plan ( Figure 11.15 , Figure 11.16 , and Figure 11.17 ).

sections.patient_teaching.3.quote: A home peak flow meter ( Figure 11.18 ) allows patients to track and observe trends in their lung function.

sections.patient_teaching.4.quote: Steroid inhalers can increase the risk of oral candida infections, so patient education should include rinsing the mouth after use, and use of spacers if indicated.
